products.name: Automation Cloud Administration and Test Cloud Administration
products.source:
* In-app notification retention is now limited to 30 days; older notifications are no longer available regardless of topic. This is rolling out progressively across regions and applies to cloud environments only.
* Administrators can now grant more than one AI and Agentic usage top-up to a user in a single action from the **User usage** dashboard, with each top-up recorded as its own consumption event.

analysis.name: Automation Cloud Administration and Test Cloud Administration
analysis.summary: Administration updates limit in-app notification retention to 30 days in cloud environments and streamline AI and Agentic usage top-up management from the User usage dashboard.
analysis.overall_analysis: These changes emphasize tighter operational controls and simpler administration for cloud tenants, with one change reducing long-term notification availability and the other making usage allocation easier to manage at scale.

changes.name: 30-day in-app notification retention
changes.summary: In-app notifications are now retained for only 30 days, and older notifications are no longer available regardless of topic. The rollout is progressive across regions and applies only to cloud environments.
changes.analysis: This likely reduces storage or operational overhead and standardizes notification lifecycle management, but it also shortens the window for reviewing past notifications.
changes.impact: Cloud environment users and administrators who rely on historical in-app notifications are affected, especially in regions receiving the rollout.

changes.name: Bulk AI and Agentic usage top-ups in one action
changes.summary: Administrators can grant more than one AI and Agentic usage top-up to a user in a single action from the User usage dashboard, and each top-up is recorded as its own consumption event.
changes.analysis: This improves administrative efficiency for managing user entitlements while preserving granular consumption tracking for auditing or reporting.

products.name: Action Center
products.source:
* A one-time Microsoft Entra admin consent is required by August 26, 2026 for actionable notifications in Outlook to keep working, following Microsoft's move away from legacy authentication for Actionable Messages.
* The Validation Station compact view adds a filter bar to search and hide fields by state (confirmed, not extracted, no flagged issues).
* Quick Form tasks are now available in public preview, letting you add human-in-the-loop tasks to any process (Maestro BPMN, Case Management, Flow, or Agents) without building or deploying an app, including inline debug support.

analysis.name: Action Center
analysis.summary: Action Center introduces an Outlook actionable notifications consent requirement, improves Validation Station compact view filtering, and adds Quick Form tasks in public preview for lightweight human-in-the-loop workflows.
analysis.overall_analysis: The updates combine a required integration maintenance step with usability improvements and a broader push to simplify human-task orchestration across multiple UiPath process surfaces.

changes.name: Microsoft Entra admin consent required for Outlook actionable notifications
changes.summary: A one-time Microsoft Entra admin consent is required by August 26, 2026 for actionable notifications in Outlook to continue working, due to Microsoft's move away from legacy authentication for Actionable Messages.
changes.analysis: This is a time-sensitive dependency update needed to maintain an existing integration as Microsoft's authentication model changes.
changes.impact: Organizations using actionable notifications in Outlook, especially Microsoft Entra administrators and Action Center users, are affected.

changes.name: Validation Station compact view filter bar
changes.summary: The Validation Station compact view now includes a filter bar that lets users search fields and hide fields by state, including confirmed, not extracted, and no flagged issues.
changes.analysis: This likely improves review efficiency by helping users focus on relevant fields during validation tasks.
changes.impact: Users working in Validation Station compact view are affected.

changes.name: Quick Form tasks public preview
changes.summary: Quick Form tasks are available in public preview, allowing human-in-the-loop tasks to be added to processes in Maestro BPMN, Case Management, Flow, or Agents without building or deploying an app. Inline debug support is included.
changes.analysis: This lowers the implementation barrier for adding human steps to workflows and may accelerate process design and testing.
changes.impact: Process designers and developers using Maestro BPMN, Case Management, Flow, or Agents are affected.

products.name: Agents
products.source:
* Agents can now retain and reuse what they learned from past executions (episodic memory) and past escalation resolutions (escalation memory), available in preview.
* Conversational agents now support personal connections in public preview, letting individual users choose which of their own Integration Service connections an agent uses on their behalf.

analysis.name: Agents
analysis.summary: Agents gain preview memory capabilities for retaining prior learning and escalation resolutions, and conversational agents now support personal connections in public preview.
analysis.overall_analysis: These changes extend agent continuity and personalization, indicating a broader move toward more context-aware and user-specific agent behavior.

changes.name: Episodic and escalation memory in preview
changes.summary: Agents can retain and reuse what they learned from past executions through episodic memory and from past escalation resolutions through escalation memory. Both capabilities are available in preview.
changes.analysis: This likely improves agent effectiveness over time by allowing recurring context and prior resolutions to inform future behavior.
changes.impact: Users building or running agents, especially those with repeated workflows or escalations, are affected.

changes.name: Personal connections for conversational agents
changes.summary: Conversational agents now support personal connections in public preview, enabling individual users to choose which of their own Integration Service connections an agent uses on their behalf.
changes.analysis: This increases flexibility and user-level control while enabling agents to act through personalized integrations rather than only shared connections.
changes.impact: Users of conversational agents and administrators managing Integration Service connection usage are affected.

analysis.summary: Integration Service adds new Snowflake Cortex authentication methods, introduces an Invoke Agent activity for Microsoft Azure AI Foundry, and makes the MCP connector generally available.

changes.name: Snowflake Cortex connector authentication expansion

changes.name: Microsoft Azure AI Foundry Invoke Agent activity

changes.name: MCP connector generally available

products.name: Automation Cloud Administration and Test Cloud Administration
products.source:
* User licenses now include a single monthly AI and Agentic usage pool shared across Autopilot, Agent Development, ScreenPlay Development, Conversational Agents, and Autopilot for Everyone, replacing the separate per-product AI entitlements. Administrators grant top-ups and monitor per-user usage from **Admin > Licenses > Consumables > User usage**.
* Transactional Billing is a new charging model for agentic solutions orchestrated by Maestro. It packages a solution run into a single, tiered transaction cost based on a universal consumption unit called an AI Step. Component-based pricing remains available in parallel, and a solution runs under one model or the other. Transactional Billing is available to organizations on Unified Pricing and is enabled per folder.
* SCIM User Sync is now generally available, synchronizing user creation, updates, and deprovisioning between UiPath and Microsoft Entra ID or Okta.
* The Community plan is now available for organizations on Unified Pricing, giving individual developers and builders free access to the UiPath agentic platform.
* The GPT-4o model version `gpt-4o-2024-05-13` will be removed from the platform on October 1, 2026, following its retirement by Microsoft. Automations and Bring Your Own (BYO) configurations that use it require migration to GPT-5.1 before the removal date.
* Organization Administrators can now use the Check access API to retrieve effective access for a user, group, or external application across the organization, including tenant-level assignments from every active tenant.
* The **Licenses** page now warns when a host-level license update no longer includes a unit type that was previously allocated to an organization. The existing allocation is preserved until you de-allocate the unit types that are no longer available. The consumables API key is also hidden by default on the **Consumables** tab.
* Firewall configuration pages were audited. Apps monitoring, Sentry, and SignalR domains were added, and obsolete or duplicate domains were removed from the Automation Cloud Portal, Action Center, Apps, Data Fabric, Document Understanding, Orchestrator, and Studio Web entries.
* Free organizations that had Legacy User License Management disabled before an Enterprise downgrade now enable User License Management automatically 14 days after the downgrade, unless you upgrade back to Enterprise within that window.

analysis.name: Automation Cloud Administration and Test Cloud Administration
analysis.summary: This release updates licensing, billing, identity sync, administration APIs, platform configuration guidance, and plan availability across Automation Cloud Administration and Test Cloud Administration. It also announces a model retirement and clarifies behavior around license allocations and downgraded organizations.
analysis.overall_analysis: The changes broaden administrative control over licensing and access, add a new pricing model for agentic solutions, and improve enterprise identity and governance capabilities. They also require some customers to plan migrations and review licensing behavior, especially around GPT-4o retirement and downgraded free organizations.

changes.name: Unified monthly AI and Agentic user usage pool
changes.summary: User licenses now include a single monthly AI and Agentic usage pool shared across Autopilot, Agent Development, ScreenPlay Development, Conversational Agents, and Autopilot for Everyone, replacing separate per-product AI entitlements. Administrators can grant top-ups and monitor per-user usage from Admin > Licenses > Consumables > User usage.
changes.analysis: This simplifies entitlement management by consolidating usage across multiple products into one pool and gives administrators clearer control over consumption and top-ups.
changes.impact: Administrators and licensed users of Autopilot, Agent Development, ScreenPlay Development, Conversational Agents, and Autopilot for Everyone are affected.

changes.name: Transactional Billing for Maestro agentic solutions
changes.summary: Transactional Billing is introduced as a new charging model for agentic solutions orchestrated by Maestro. It prices a solution run as a single, tiered transaction based on an AI Step universal consumption unit, while component-based pricing remains available in parallel. A solution run uses one model or the other. This is available to organizations on Unified Pricing and is enabled per folder.
changes.analysis: This provides an alternative pricing approach for agentic solutions, which may make costs easier to reason about at the solution-run level while preserving the existing component-based option.
changes.impact: Organizations on Unified Pricing using Maestro-orchestrated agentic solutions, especially administrators configuring billing per folder, are affected.

changes.name: SCIM User Sync generally available
changes.summary: SCIM User Sync is now generally available for synchronizing user creation, updates, and deprovisioning between UiPath and Microsoft Entra ID or Okta.
changes.analysis: General availability indicates the feature is production-ready for identity lifecycle automation, reducing manual user administration.
changes.impact: Organizations using Microsoft Entra ID or Okta for identity management and administrators responsible for provisioning are affected.

changes.name: Community plan on Unified Pricing
changes.summary: The Community plan is now available for organizations on Unified Pricing, giving individual developers and builders free access to the UiPath agentic platform.
changes.analysis: This expands access to the platform for individual builders within the Unified Pricing model and may encourage adoption and experimentation.
changes.impact: Individual developers, builders, and organizations using Unified Pricing are affected.

changes.name: GPT-4o model retirement notice
changes.summary: The GPT-4o model version `gpt-4o-2024-05-13` will be removed from the platform on October 1, 2026, following its retirement by Microsoft. Automations and Bring Your Own (BYO) configurations that use it must migrate to GPT-5.1 before the removal date.
changes.analysis: This is a time-bound compatibility and continuity issue that requires customers to identify dependencies and migrate before the model is removed.
changes.impact: Customers using `gpt-4o-2024-05-13` in automations or BYO configurations are affected.

changes.name: Check access API for effective access retrieval
changes.summary: Organization Administrators can now use the Check access API to retrieve effective access for a user, group, or external application across the organization, including tenant-level assignments from every active tenant.
changes.analysis: This improves visibility into permissions and supports governance, auditing, and troubleshooting of complex access setups.

Existing allocation remains until those no-longer-available unit types are de-allocated. The consumables API key is now hidden by default on the Consumables tab.

changes.analysis: This helps customers maintain accurate allowlists and network configurations, which can reduce connectivity or monitoring issues caused by outdated documentation.
changes.impact: Network administrators and customers maintaining firewall allowlists for the listed services are affected.

changes.analysis: This defines post-downgrade behavior and a transition period, helping standardize license management after plan changes.

products.name: Action Center
products.source:
* The Actions list replaces the **Timer Status** filter with a multi-select **Due Status** filter, covering **Due later**, **Due soon**, **Overdue**, **No timer**, and **Completed in time** on the **Completed** tab. It also adds a **Due Time** filter and sort, and each action row shows its due status with the completion due date in a tooltip.
* Timers configured with **Task assigned** as the end criteria no longer appear in the interface. They continue to run, and their configured outcome still triggers when they expire.
* A future release will change the **Due soon** threshold from 80% of the completion timer duration to a fixed 24 hours remaining. Completion timers shorter than 24 hours will then report **Due soon** for their entire duration.
* Document Validation and Document Classification actions add a **Report a technical issue** button. Reports can attach an anonymized copy of the taxonomy and the extraction or classification result, and never capture the document or the text values read from it.
* When a Document Validation action opens in the classic view, the Validation Station now offers to switch to the compact view and back. The choice is remembered per reviewer and browser.
* The document viewer used by Document Validation and Document Classification actions was updated to pick up upstream security fixes, and now requires a more recent browser. In older browsers, the document fails to load and an error is displayed in its place.

analysis.name: Action Center
analysis.summary: This release updates due-date filtering and due-status visibility, changes how some timers appear, adds issue reporting in document actions, improves classic-to-compact view switching, and updates the document viewer with newer browser requirements. It also announces a future Due soon threshold change.
analysis.overall_analysis: The release focuses on usability for action management and document review while also introducing a browser compatibility constraint through a security-related viewer update. Teams should prepare for both the announced future due-status logic change and the newer browser requirement.

changes.analysis: This makes action tracking and filtering more precise, helping users prioritize work and review completion timeliness more effectively.

products.name: Agents
products.source:
* Agents can now use coded functions as tools. The coded function tool, available in preview, runs custom Python code as a deterministic, process-based tool, so an agent can reason over the structured result.
* Conversational agents support client-side tools, which execute on the user's browser or host application rather than on the UiPath server. This lets agents access client-local data, trigger UI actions, and use device capabilities.
* The **gemini-3.5-flash** model is now available for Agents.

products.source:
* The new **IXP Project Creator** role grants the **Project - Create** permission, which lets a user create IXP projects in the tenant without a service or organization administrator role. The user who creates a project becomes project admin of that project automatically.
* Custom roles can now include four tenant-level project permissions: **Project - Create**, **Project - Read**, **Project - Write**, and **Project - Delete**. Each one applies to every project in the tenant.
* New IXP projects, both Communications Mining and Unstructured and Complex Documents, now include the **Administrators** group as **IXP Project Admin** from the moment they are created.
* In Unstructured and Complex Documents projects, importing and exporting taxonomies now requires **Dataset - Review** instead of **Dataset - Write**. **Dataset - Write** now gates updating a project's **Model configuration** settings.
* Generative AI features in Communications Mining are now recorded in the UiPath AI Trust Layer audit log.
* At the end of a batch in **Check label** or **Missed label** training mode, you can now continue with the next messages in the sort order instead of returning to the **Train** page.

products.name: Orchestrator
products.source:
* Google Cloud Storage is available as a new storage bucket provider, authenticated with a service account key.
* Azure Storage buckets can be authenticated with Integration Service service-principal connections instead of storage-account access keys, so security teams can enforce Entra-based identity and access management policies.
* The default API specification is now the OpenAPI 3.0 Public profile. The previous V20 specification, based on Swagger 2.0, is deprecated as of this release and will be removed in September 2026.
* The tenant-level **Jobs** view now offers every column available in folder-level **Jobs** views, including Started/Ended, Creation Time, Source, Priority, Machine, Hostname, User interaction, and Healing Agent status. All added columns are hidden by default.
* Side panels render on top of primary content instead of pushing it aside. They are resizable, keep the chosen width for the session, and leave the underlying grid or list interactive.
* For queue triggers on Maestro processes, **Minimum number of items to trigger the first job** and **Another job is triggered after each** are now fixed to **1**.
* Automation Cloud Robots - Serverless in the United States delayed update (GxP) region support static IPs. Enable the option in your serverless robot template, then add the corresponding IPs to your allowlist.
* Automation Cloud Robots - Serverless in the Japan region now run redundantly across Japan East and Japan West, which adds outbound IP ranges you must allowlist if you restrict serverless robot traffic. Data residency is unchanged.

analysis.name: Orchestrator
analysis.summary: Orchestrator adds new storage authentication options, updates the default API specification, expands the tenant-level Jobs view, changes side-panel behavior, adjusts Maestro queue trigger settings, and updates Automation Cloud Robots - Serverless networking details for the United States delayed update (GxP) and Japan regions.
analysis.overall_analysis: These changes emphasize stronger security and standards alignment, a more capable and less disruptive UI, and clearer operational requirements for serverless robots across regions. They also signal upcoming API migration work because the previous V20 specification is deprecated and scheduled for removal in September 2026.

products.name: Test Manager
products.source:
* Performance Testing adds a Workflow Analyzer that scans an automation before a run starts and flags unsupported activities and Studio version or activity-package mismatches, so problems surface before robot minutes are spent.
* Capacity Planner runs a short series of safe load probes against your actual hardware and extrapolates a data-backed virtual-user recommendation, with guardrails that keep it within limits already proven safe on your infrastructure.
* Elastic Robot Pools generate load from your own Azure, AWS, or Google Cloud capacity instead of shared, multi-tenant infrastructure, scaling load injectors up and down as a test requires.
* When port 5671 is blocked, Performance Testing falls back to WebSocket communication over port 443, and then to API-based metric delivery, so metrics no longer depend on a new firewall rule.
* Robot logs are viewable and filterable, by load group and by severity, directly inside the Performance Testing results screen, alongside application logs.
* Every performance test run generates a dedicated report view for each stakeholder who acts on the result: Program Managers, Developers, InfraOps, and QA/Testers.
* GPT-4o is deprecated in Autopilot, with support ending October 31, 2026. Switch to a supported alternative model in your AI Trust Layer policy before then to avoid disruption to test generation, quality checks, and other Autopilot capabilities.

analysis.name: Test Manager
analysis.summary: Test Manager adds multiple Performance Testing enhancements, including pre-run analysis, hardware-based capacity planning, elastic load generation from customer cloud infrastructure, communication fallbacks, integrated log viewing, and stakeholder-specific reports. It also announces the deprecation of GPT-4o in Autopilot, with support ending October 31, 2026.
analysis.overall_analysis: These updates significantly strengthen performance testing maturity by improving readiness checks, scaling flexibility, observability, and reporting, while the GPT-4o deprecation requires planning to avoid disruption in Autopilot-dependent testing workflows.

changes.name: Workflow Analyzer for Performance Testing
changes.summary: Performance Testing adds a Workflow Analyzer that scans an automation before a run starts and flags unsupported activities and Studio version or activity-package mismatches.
changes.analysis: This helps teams catch compatibility and support issues before execution, reducing wasted robot minutes and failed runs.
changes.impact: Affects users preparing performance tests and teams responsible for automation compatibility.

changes.name: Capacity Planner with safe load probes
changes.summary: Capacity Planner runs a short series of safe load probes against actual hardware and extrapolates a data-backed virtual-user recommendation, while keeping recommendations within limits already proven safe on the infrastructure.
changes.analysis: This gives teams a more evidence-based way to size tests and infrastructure usage while limiting the risk of overloading environments.
changes.impact: Affects performance engineers, infrastructure teams, and testers planning performance test scale.

changes.name: Elastic Robot Pools using customer cloud capacity
changes.summary: Elastic Robot Pools generate load from the customer's own Azure, AWS, or Google Cloud capacity instead of shared multi-tenant infrastructure, scaling load injectors up and down as required by the test.
changes.analysis: This provides more control over performance test infrastructure and may better align testing with customer-specific cloud environments and scaling needs.
changes.impact: Affects organizations running performance tests that need dedicated or cloud-controlled load generation.

changes.name: Port 443 and API fallback for Performance Testing metrics

changes.analysis: This improves reliability in restricted network environments and reduces the need for new firewall rules to obtain metrics.
changes.impact: Affects users running Performance Testing in environments with stricter firewall settings.

changes.analysis: This improves troubleshooting efficiency by centralizing key diagnostics within the results experience.
changes.impact: Affects developers, testers, and operations teams analyzing performance test outcomes.

changes.name: Stakeholder-specific performance test reports
changes.summary: Every performance test run now generates a dedicated report view for each stakeholder who acts on the result: Program Managers, Developers, InfraOps, and QA/Testers.
changes.analysis: This likely improves communication and decision-making by tailoring result views to different audiences and responsibilities.
changes.impact: Affects all teams that review performance test results across product, engineering, infrastructure, and QA functions.

changes.name: Maestro Case and Maestro Flow project types added

changes.name: Queue support and Base64 file-conversion activities for API workflows
